agency.name: Wyoming Department of Workforce Services, Workers' Compensation Division

ttd.basisLabel: Gross monthly wage at the time of injury
ttd.rateText: TTD is paid monthly at 30% of the statewide average monthly wage or two-thirds of the employee's actual monthly earnings at the time of injury, whichever is greater, but not more than the lesser of 100% of the employee's actual monthly earnings or the statewide average monthly wage for the 12 months preceding the quarter of injury; half is paid around the 15th and half around the 30th of the month (Wyo. Stat. § 27-14-403(c)).
ttd.minText: Minimum = 30% of the statewide average monthly wage ($1,686.10 for injuries in 2026 Q4), but never more than 100% of the worker's actual monthly earnings (§ 27-14-403(c)).
ttd.periodLabel: injuries in the fourth quarter of 2026 (October-December 2026); the rate changes every quarter (2026 Q3: max $5,204.33, min $1,561.30); weekly equivalents of the monthly limits ($5,620.33 a month × 12 ÷ 52)

waiting.text: Disability payments are not allowed for the first three days of disability unless the incapacity extends beyond eight days; the day of injury counts unless full wages were paid for it, and no employee can be forced to use sick leave first (Wyo. Stat. § 27-14-404(d)).

ttdDuration.text: TTD for any one incident may not exceed a cumulative 24 months, unless the Division awards more in extraordinary circumstances (Wyo. Stat. § 27-14-404(a)). The statute counts months, not weeks.

ppd.text: Permanent partial impairment is rated under the most recent AMA Guides and paid monthly at two-thirds of the statewide average monthly wage for (impairment % x 60) months (Wyo. Stat. §§ 27-14-403(c), 27-14-405(g)). A worker who cannot return to work at 95% of pre-injury earnings and has actively sought work may then claim a permanent partial disability award based on age, education and work history (§ 27-14-405(h)-(j)).

facts.text: Wyoming's benefit caps change every quarter, because they are tied to the statewide average monthly wage for the 12 months before the quarter of injury (§ 27-14-403(c)).

Wyoming workers' compensation claims are handled by the state Department of Workforce Services, which assigns a nine-digit claim number; the injury must be reported to the employer within 72 hours and to the Division within 10 days.

In permanent total disability or death cases each child receives $250.00 a month (payments after July 1, 2009), adjusted annually for inflation by the lesser of CPI or 3%, until age 21 (25 if in post-secondary education) (§ 27-14-403(b)).
Temporary light duty is paid at 80% of the difference between the light-duty wage and pre-injury monthly earnings (§ 27-14-403(c)).
A worker cannot receive TTD while receiving unemployment compensation (§ 27-14-404(d)(iii)).
